EU flash consumer confidence: -15.8, down 0.8 points from August.

Quick analysis: Consumers had been feeling gradually better, but September’s reading suggests that improvement has stalled.

Weaker confidence may weigh on household spending and is a growth consideration for the European Central Bank.

The euro could face some pressure from the softer reading, although inflation and other economic data will also shape the bank’s decisions.
